method: Independent lens review of captured evidence. The director opened every screenshot for a surface before scoring it, read the axe and capture results, and scored without sight of any other director's scores.
overallNote: Through the visual design and art direction lens this is clearly designed work — one restrained palette with indigo as a single accent, a consistent small-caps label register, and real display typography on Timeline, About and Landing. Nothing here is template-default. What keeps every surface below the 9.5 floor is grid and edge discipline rather than taste: left edges that don't hold (Notes' composer at x=310 against a panel at x=276 against list text at x=336; the RESOURCES block breaking the task modal's x=201 column; the wordmark at x=122 against Landing's x=283 hero), a marketing site running three different page margins across three pages, unequal cells in Pricing's three-up band, and column headers that don't align to the content they label in the Tasks list. There are also two cross-surface inconsistencies a system should not permit: the same user rendered as an orange square in the list and a purple circle in the detail modal, and the marketing body grey reading warmer than the app's cool neutrals. The Tasks list clipping its Priority column at 1440 is the closest thing to a defect a reviewer would call out immediately, but it is truncation at a scroll edge, not something disqualifying — I am not casting a veto on any surface. The strongest work is Timeline, whose mobile vertical rail is a genuine re-composition rather than a squeeze; the weakest is the Tasks list view, where two typographic registers, doubled row controls and a clipped column pile up in one table. Standing caveat: these are static captures. Motion, hover, focus, drag and empty/loading/error states outside the two captured per surface are unverifiable here, and I have given them no credit in any score.

surfaces.rationale: Board is the stronger half: five columns on an even ~201px/27px gutter rhythm, restrained neutral palette, and column descriptions ('Agreed and ready to start.', 'In motion right now.') that are clearly written, not default. Two real faults. First, the description block has no fixed height, so 'Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision.' wraps to two lines and drops the Waiting column's 'Nothing held up' card ~14px below the first card in every sibling column — the board's top card row does not align. Second, Done is the only tinted column: five green-filled cards plus green checks stack into the heaviest colour field on the screen, so the strongest visual weight sits on finished work. The List view is weaker. At 1440 the Priority column is clipped at the viewport edge — the header reads 'P' and values render 'Hig…', 'Lo…', 'No…' truncated mid-word. Every row carries two near-identical adjacent controls (square checkbox at x=316, circle at x=346) with no labelling to separate select from complete. The ALL-CAPS letterspaced header labels (TASK, STATUS, OWNER, DATES) don't align to the content beneath them — OWNER sits at x=1128 over avatars at x=1101, DATES at x=1287 over values at x=1266 — and the group rows mix a monospace face ('3 tasks', '0/3 done') into a sans header, which reads as debug output. Empty states are inconsistent between views of the same data: the board gives Waiting a designed 'Nothing held up' card, the list gives it unstyled grey text. The orange 'OR' avatar repeats 13 times down the Owner column as the table's only warm hue. On mobile, three stacked horizontal scrollers (view tabs, filter row, column chips) plus the header push the first card to y≈380 of 844 — 45% of the screen is chrome before content, and the bottom bar mixes products (Home, Notes, Tasks, Timeline) with a view switcher ('Board ⌄') in one row. Static captures cannot show me drag, hover, or column-reorder states, so I have given no credit for them.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Fix the List view's right-edge clipping so the Priority column is never truncated at 1440, and align the ALL-CAPS column headers to the cell content they label; then normalise the board's column-description block to a fixed height so the first card row aligns across all five columns.

surfaces.rationale: The modal has a real structure — a 26px semibold title, a right metadata rail on a consistent ~35px group rhythm (REPEATS / TAGS / CONTACT / PROJECT / SOURCE / COPIES / ADD FIELD), and a single small-caps letterspaced label register used throughout. Alignment breaks in the left column: DESCRIPTION and CONVERSATION both start at x=201, but RESOURCES is inset to x=222 with its dropzone spanning 225–851 against the 201–875 of its siblings, so one section's left edge doesn't hold the line. Dividers are applied unevenly — rules sit under Description, under Add subtask, and above the reply row, but none between Resources and Conversation. The vertical column rule stops at y=740 while the modal continues to y=805, reading as an accidental termination, and the modal is taller than its content: roughly 150px of dead space sits below both columns on a task this light. Colour discipline fails across surfaces rather than within: Orla is an orange rounded square in the List view and a purple circle here — same person, two colours and two shapes. 'DRAFT A REPLY' uses the all-caps letterspaced treatment that the page otherwise reserves for section headers, so a button collides with the label register. On mobile the status/owner/date/priority chip row wraps and strands 'Mark done' alone on a second line, making a ragged block, and a small dark rounded shape bleeds at the very top of the sheet (x≈95–180, y≈0–8) that reads as a clipping artefact. Open/close motion and hover states are outside what these captures can show, so I score only the static composition.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Pull the RESOURCES block back to the x=201 left edge shared by DESCRIPTION and CONVERSATION, apply the section dividers consistently, and unify the Orla avatar to one colour and one shape across list, board and detail.

surfaces.rationale: Good bones: a well-judged composer with a placeholder in the brand's voice ('Write the thought before it disappears…'), a clearly marked selected row (indigo tint plus a 3px indigo bar at x=276), and two disciplined chip tints ('In Tasks' green, 'To review' lavender). The alignment is the problem. Three left edges stack in the same visual column: the composer card begins at x=310, the search/list panel at x=276, and list-item text at x=336 — the composer is centred in the content area while the list below is a two-pane layout on different bounds, so nothing lines up top to bottom. The 'Private to you' + overflow cluster (x=830–966) is neither left-aligned, right-aligned, nor centred on the viewport (750) or the reading pane (932); it floats against no edge. The reading pane has no typographic hierarchy at all — the note renders as one 19px paragraph with the metadata footer pinned to the bottom, leaving roughly 300px of empty white between them, so the pane reads as an unfilled container rather than a designed document. In the list, every 'To review' row grows a band of three outlined buttons (Keep / Turn into task / Delete), which repeatedly breaks the scanning rhythm and gives a red destructive action the same visual weight as the two safe ones. On mobile the active 'Notebook' tab's grey background runs flush to x=0 with its left corners squared off — the pill is clipped at the viewport edge. Voice capture and photo states are not in evidence and I have assumed nothing about them.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Put the composer, the search row and the list on one shared left edge, and give the reading pane a real type hierarchy (a note heading distinct from body) instead of a single paragraph size in a large empty box.

surfaces.rationale: The most art-directed surface in the set. 'Mara & Finn' at ~86px against a 15px eyebrow and a 19px subhead is a genuine three-step editorial hierarchy, the '79 days' stat block rags cleanly to x=1380 with a hairline above and an underlined '2 of 9 complete', and the hero left edge at x=120 is held by the axis below it. The mobile version is a real re-composition, not a squeeze — the horizontal axis becomes a vertical rail with the same dot language. Where it falls down is the axis itself. The right third degenerates: eight near-identical circles between x=1063 and x=1329, two stray thin vertical strokes at x=1140 and x=1195 that belong to no established mark language, and a '4 milestones' bracket standing in for labels — all in the region the reader most needs to read, while the month ticks stop at 'Jul' even though the timeline runs to 3 Oct. The upper milestone labels each relate to their dot differently: 'We said yes' is left-aligned at its dot, 'Menu tasting at The Orchard' is centred on its, and 'Wedding day' (centre 1273) sits well off its dot at 1329 — meanwhile the two lower labels are correctly centred, so the inconsistency is visible in one glance. In the header, Preview and Share sit adjacent with clearly different corner radii (rounded rect vs full pill), and the Timeline/Milestones segmented control is ambiguous, with the grey-filled 'Milestones' reading as selected against the white 'Timeline'. 'Wedding day · 3 Oct · 79 days to go' in the breadcrumb duplicates the hero stat verbatim, diluting the display moment.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Redesign the right end of the axis — extend the month scale through Oct, space or cluster the upcoming dots deliberately, drop the two stray tick strokes, and put every milestone label in one consistent alignment relationship to its dot.

surfaces.rationale: The typography carries this. A ~112px headline set tight, with 'Project', 'management' and 'people' all holding a clean x=283 left edge, and exactly one colour event on the page — 'outside' in indigo — is disciplined art direction, not decoration. The two buttons match in height and radius, and the monospace 'NOTES → TASKS → TIMELINE' eyebrow ties back to the mono numerals used inside the app, so the accent face is a system rather than a one-off. Two things hold it below the bar. The wordmark sits at x=122 while the hero column starts at x=283 — the nav runs on a wider container than the content, so 'signal studio.' hangs 161px outside the grid the headline establishes, and there is no counterweight on the right half of the hero. And the first viewport is type-only: the headline block ends around y=700, then roughly 140px of undifferentiated white runs to the section rule at y=838, with no product shown at all on a product landing page. Mobile repeats the same trailing void between the mono eyebrow and the divider. Minor but visible: the wordmark's trailing period reads black on desktop and indigo on mobile. Scroll behaviour, motion and any hero animation are outside what a static capture shows, and I have given no credit for them.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Put the wordmark on the same left edge as the hero headline so the page runs on one grid, and give the first viewport a visual counterweight — actual product, not more white — instead of ending on a void.

surfaces.rationale: A confident editorial page. The indigo hairline rail at x=96 with a dot at its head is a real device rather than ornament — on mobile it earns its place, sprouting a node and connector at y≈782 to introduce 'A wedding may be the largest project someone ever manages.' at a step up in size, and the bolded pull-line 'The mistake was assuming every project should work that way.' gives the body copy a genuine second level. The 72px four-line headline holds a clean left edge at x=124 under the eyebrow, and the off-white ground separates the page from the white landing without inventing a new palette. The desktop first viewport is where it weakens: the body paragraph is placed far right (x=733–1320) while the entire lower left (x=124–730, y=620–900) is empty, so the composition reads as a two-column grid missing its left column, with ~600px of nothing between headline and copy and no node hanging off the rail to justify it in that screen. The measure at that width runs long for 19px text. The body grey reads noticeably warmer than the cool neutrals used in the app, which is a cross-surface colour inconsistency. On mobile the rail (x=10), the node circle (x=32) and the heading left edge (x=24) form three near-but-not-equal verticals at the same junction.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Resolve the desktop first viewport — either bring the body copy back onto the headline's column or give the empty left half something structural to hold, so the rail reads as a grid rather than decoration.

surfaces.rationale: The hero is well set — indigo mono 'PRICING' eyebrow, a ~68px two-line headline, and the following section head at x=161 holding the same left edge. The three-up trust strip beneath it is the concrete failure. The band is full-bleed but its cells are unequal: dividers at x=533 and x=907 make the outer cells 533px and the middle one 374px. The insets are worse than the widths — 'No charge' is inset 161px from the band's left edge to match the page margin, while 'VAT included' and 'Terms repeated' sit only 28px off their dividers, so three items meant to read as a set have wildly different left gaps and no shared grid. Across the marketing site the page margin never settles: landing's hero starts at x=283, about at x=124, pricing at x=161 — three sibling pages, three different content edges. Composition also costs the page its job: the first desktop screen contains the headline, a subhead, the trust strip and a second headline, and no prices. That also limits what I can score — the plan cards, the single most design-critical element on a pricing page, are entirely below the fold and absent from this evidence, so I have assumed nothing about their spacing, hierarchy or colour and scored conservatively. Mobile handles the same band better, stacking it as three hairline-separated rows on a consistent 22px inset.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Rebuild the three-up trust strip on an even grid with equal cells and matching insets, and settle one shared content margin across landing, about and pricing so the three pages read as one site.
